title: Rate–distortion tradeoff for distributed lossy source coding
formal: Determine \[F_{\mathrm{RD}}(P,d_1,d_2,D_1,D_2,\lambda)=\inf_{(R_1,R_2)\in\mathcal R(P,d_1,d_2,D_1,D_2)}\bigl(\lambda R_1+(1-\lambda)R_2\bigr)\] for every finite-alphabet memoryless source pair, finite distortion tables, feasible distortion targets and \(\lambda\in[0,1]\), where \(\mathcal R\) is the rate region for separate encoders and a joint decoder.
why: The basic unresolved limit of compressing correlated information without coordination between encoders.

progress.text: The model notes present Berger–Tung inner and outer bounds and state that the general distributed lossy rate–distortion region is not known.

definitions: The source alphabets \(\mathcal X_i\) and reproduction alphabets \(\widehat{\mathcal X}_i\), for \(i=1,2\), are nonempty finite sets. The pairs \((X_{1,t},X_{2,t})\) are independent identically distributed draws from an arbitrary real probability table \(P\) on \(\mathcal X_1\times\mathcal X_2\). Distortions are finite-valued functions \(d_i:\mathcal X_i\times\widehat{\mathcal X}_i\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}\). Write \(P_i\) for the marginal source law and \(D_{i,\min}=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X_i}P_i(x)\min_{z\in\widehat{\mathcal X}_i}d_i(x,z)\). The domain requires finite real \(D_i\ge D_{i,\min}\). An \(n\)-block code consists of deterministic encoders \(f_{i,n}:\mathcal X_i^n\to[M_{i,n}]\), where \([M]=\{1,\ldots,M\}\) and \(M_{i,n}\ge1\), and a deterministic decoder from the pair of indices to \(\widehat{\mathcal X}_1^n\times\widehat{\mathcal X}_2^n\). Each encoder sees only its own source block. For the resulting reproductions define \(\Delta_{i,n}=n^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^n\mathbb E[d_i(X_{i,t},\widehat X_{i,t})]\). A nonnegative pair is achievable if, along some \(n_j\to\infty\), codes satisfy \(\limsup_{j\to\infty}n_j^{-1}\log_2M_{i,n_j}\le R_i\) and \(\limsup_{j\to\infty}\Delta_{i,n_j}\le D_i\) for both sources. The region \(\mathcal R\) is the closure of achievable pairs. There is no interaction, extra side information, computational restriction or variable-length encoding; distortion is expected per-symbol distortion. Predetermined time sharing is allowed. Transmitting both source blocks and selecting minimum-distortion reproductions establishes feasibility on the stated domain; smaller distortion targets, which would give an empty region, are excluded. The region is convex and upward closed. Its nonnegative lower supporting values describe its lower rate boundary. The target is finite and nonnegative, in weighted bits per source pair. All tables are mathematical real objects, with no algorithmic representation requirement.
answer_criterion: Supply an unambiguous real-valued function \(g\) on the whole source, distortion and weight domain above and a Lean proof of \(|g-F_{\mathrm{RD}}|\le1/100\) pointwise. This is an error bound on the weighted rate in bits per source pair; the distortion constraints remain exact. Prove both sides of the bound, or determine the function exactly. A finite sample of values or a restatement of the operational infimum or limit is insufficient. No specified formula grammar or polynomial evaluation-time requirement is imposed.

sentences: Two encoders separately compress correlated source blocks for one joint decoder.
Each reconstructed source must satisfy its own expected per-symbol distortion limit.
The function records the smallest weighted sum of the two description rates.
Only feasible distortion targets are included, so every requested value is finite.
The benchmark keeps the distortion constraints exact and requires a Lean-certified rate error of at most 0.01 on the whole domain.

context_blocks.text: Separate encoders describe correlated source blocks to one decoder. Correlation can reduce the total communication even though the encoders cannot inspect each other’s data. Allowing distortion changes the problem from lossless reconstruction.

The historical notes give inner and outer bounds and identify the general two-source lossy region as unresolved. This card measures its lower boundary by the minimum weighted rate and explicitly excludes infeasible distortion targets.
